items.title: A continuous finite-variation martingale is constant
items.statement: A continuous finite-variation martingale on a finite horizon with integrable total variation and initial value zero is indistinguishably zero.
items.strategy: Localize by total variation; prove the stopped process remains a martingale by deterministic step approximations, then use orthogonal increments and vanishing squared-increment sums.

items.title: Bounded stopping preserves càdlàg square-integrable martingales
items.statement: If M is a càdlàg square-integrable all-pairs martingale on a finite horizon and τ≤T is a stopping time, then M_{t∧τ} is a square-integrable martingale.
items.strategy: Approximate τ from above by finite-valued grid stopping times, prove the finite-grid assertion by predictable increments, and pass to the limit using right continuity and a sampled Doob bound.

items.title: Simple counting-process intensity and compensator contract
items.statement: On a finite horizon define a simple unit-jump counting process, a predictable at-risk process and nonnegative predictable intensity through A_t=∫_0^t Y_s λ_s ds, with A continuous, predictable, A_0=0, E[A_T]<∞, and M=N−A assumed by model contract to be a square-integrable martingale.
items.strategy: Specify the finite-horizon objects and the model contract; explicitly make no general compensator-existence claim from an intensity display.

items.title: Optional and predictable brackets for counting-process martingales
items.statement: For the finite-variation martingales in this model define optional covariation by the jump-square sum and predictable brackets as the unique continuous predictable finite-variation compensators when they exist.
items.strategy: Fix the finite-horizon jump-sum and compensator conventions; the assigned bracket theorem proves existence for the stated model.

items.title: Elementary predictable integral against a counting-process martingale
items.statement: For a bounded predictable step integrand H=Σ_j H_j 1_(t_j,t_{j+1}] with H_j measurable at t_j, define the integral by the finite sum of H_j times the corresponding increments of M.
items.strategy: State the time-zero convention and finite-sum formula for each t≤T.

items.title: Predictable step processes are dense for the compensator L² norm
items.statement: For μ(E)=E∫_0^T 1_E dA on the predictable sigma-algebra, bounded predictable step processes are dense in L²(μ), and time zero is μ-null.
items.strategy: Show μ is finite; use the predictable interval generators, Dynkin's π–λ theorem, and density of simple functions in L².

items.title: L² counting-process integral when the limit exists
items.statement: For predictable H with E∫_0^T H² dA<∞, write ∫_0^t H dM for the L² limit of elementary step integrals when that limit exists; the following theorem proves existence, uniqueness and the isometry.
items.strategy: Define the notation conditionally on existence so no unproved completion claim is used as a supplier.

items.title: Uniqueness of continuous predictable brackets
items.statement: Two continuous predictable finite-variation processes with integrable total variation and the same martingale-compensator property are indistinguishable.
items.strategy: Subtract the two decompositions and apply the continuous finite-variation martingale lemma.

items.title: Elementary predictable counting-process integrals are martingales
items.statement: For bounded predictable step H, the finite-sum process ∫_0^t H dM is a square-integrable martingale on [0,T].
items.strategy: Check adaptedness and square integrability termwise; condition each future martingale increment on its left endpoint and test the conditional identity on events.

items.title: Finite-variation integration by parts for counting-process martingales
items.statement: For the finite-variation càdlàg paths in this model, M_t²−M_0²=2∫_0^t M_{s−}dM_s+[M]_t, with [M] the jump-square sum.
items.strategy: Use the telescoping finite-partition square identity and prove convergence of the squared-increment sums by finite-jump truncation and finite variation.

items.title: Brackets of a compensated simple counting process
items.statement: Under the finite-horizon model contract, [M]_t=N_t and the continuous predictable bracket is ⟨M⟩_t=A_t; moreover M²−A is a martingale.
items.strategy: Identify the jump-square sum, stop M, use elementary step-integral martingales and the finite-partition square identity, then pass to M²−N by dominated convergence and use bracket uniqueness.

items.title: Cross brackets vanish without simultaneous jumps
items.statement: For finitely many simple counting processes on a common filtration with continuous compensators and no simultaneous jumps, every distinct pair has zero optional and predictable cross bracket; independence is not required.
items.strategy: The continuous compensators do not change jumps; pairwise disjoint unit jumps make every optional cross jump product zero, and zero has zero predictable compensator.

items.title: Isometry for elementary predictable counting-process integrals
items.statement: For bounded predictable step H, ∫_0^t H dM is a square-integrable martingale and E(∫_0^T H dM)²=E∫_0^T H² dA.
items.strategy: Expand the finite sum; distinct martingale increments are orthogonal, and M²−A gives the conditional second-moment identity on each step.

items.title: L² extension of the predictable counting-process integral
items.statement: Every predictable H with E∫_0^T H²dA<∞ has a unique integral defined by L² completion of elementary step integrals; its process is a square-integrable martingale and E(∫_0^T H dM)²=E∫_0^T H²dA.
items.strategy: Use predictable-step density and the elementary isometry to obtain a unique L² limit, pass the isometry to the limit, and use L² continuity of conditional expectation for the martingale identity.

items.title: Delayed entry with a predictable risk process
items.statement: For a subject entering at fixed L and failing at L+E with E exponential, Y_t=1{L<t≤L+E} is predictable and A_t=λ((t−L)^+∧E) is its continuous compensator under the stated one-event model.
items.strategy: Check the left-open entry and right-closed event conventions, then use the exponential survival law conditionally on the event-free history.

items.title: A tied jump produces a nonzero cross bracket
items.statement: If two subjects share the same exponential event time, their compensated counting martingales have [M¹,M²]=N and ⟨M¹,M²⟩=A, so the no-simultaneous-jump hypothesis cannot be dropped.
items.strategy: Take the two processes equal, apply the one-process bracket result, and verify the common jump has positive probability on every positive horizon.

items.title: One exponential event: compensator and isometry
items.statement: For E exponential with rate λ, N_t=1{E≤t}, Y_t=1{t≤E}, and A_t=λ(t∧E), the compensated process is a square-integrable martingale and the constant integrand H=1 gives E[M_T²]=E[A_T]=1−e^(−λT).
items.strategy: Verify the all-pairs martingale identity by conditioning on whether the event has occurred, then evaluate the compensator expectation and apply the bounded-step isometry.
